model_organism.citation: Zebrafish dscaml1 Deficiency Impairs Retinal Patterning and Oculomotor Function (PMID: 31685652)
phenotypes: Deficits in retinal patterning and light adaptation
Severe fatigue during gaze stabilization
Reduced saccade amplitude and velocity in the light
Greater eye disconjugacy
Impaired fixation
Impaired saccade-command signals in abducens neurons (saccadic premotor pathway)
Normal abducens activation by the pretectum-vestibular pathway
Phenotypes reminiscent of human ocular motor apraxia

model_organism.citation: Fuerst et al. 2009 - DSCAM and DSCAML1 function in self-avoidance in multiple cell types in the developing mouse retina (PMID: 19945391)
phenotypes: Dscaml1 mutant retina: fasciculated rod bipolar cell dendrites
Dscaml1 mutant retina: clumped AII amacrine cell bodies, indicating a self-avoidance defect
Appropriate stratification of neurites in inner plexiform layer synaptic laminae
Functional synapses formed in the rod circuit
Dscam-/- mice: RGC dendrite fasciculation and clumped cell bodies

model_organism.citation: The rod synapse in aging wildtype and Dscaml1 mutant mice (PMID: 37910517)
phenotypes: Rod-to-rod bipolar cell synapses form and are maintained
Increased number of invaginating neurites in rod spherules
Reduced rod bipolar cell dendritic tips
Reduced mitochondrial volume and complexity in rod bipolar cells
Precocious sprouting of rod bipolar cell dendrites into the outer nuclear layer

model_organism.citation: Subtle Roles of Down Syndrome Cell Adhesion Molecules in Embryonic Forebrain Development and Neuronal Migration (PMID: 33585465)
phenotypes: Constitutive loss of Dscaml1 (Dscaml1 GT) and Dscam did not significantly affect cortical development
No significant effect on ventral forebrain morphogenesis
No significant effect on cortical interneuron migration
No significant effect on cortical-subcortical connectivity formation
Gain of function impaired neural migration and altered neuronal morphology

model_organism.citation: Deficiency in the cell-adhesion molecule dscaml1 impairs hypothalamic CRH neuron development and perturbs normal neuroendocrine stress axis function (PMID: 36875755)
phenotypes: Higher crhb expression in hypothalamic CRH neurons
Increased CRH neuron cell number
Reduced cell death in CRH neurons
Higher baseline cortisol levels
Attenuated cortisol responses to acute stressors
Dysregulated HPA axis

model_organism.citation: Pharmacological Correction of Aberrant DSCAML1 Localization by 4-Phenylbutyrate Ameliorates Epileptic Phenotypes in a Mouse Model Harboring the Patient-Specific A2105T Mutation (PMID: 42003794)
phenotypes: Dscaml1 A2105T/A2105T knock-in: mutant protein accumulates intracellularly and is not properly localized to the cell surface
Dendritic retraction in cortical layer V pyramidal neurons
Abnormal clustering of somatostatin-positive interneurons in the hippocampus
Epileptic spike-and-wave discharges
4PBA restored cell-surface localization and ameliorated neuronal deficits and reduced spike-and-wave discharge frequency

model_organism.citation: Structural Neural Connectivity Analysis in Zebrafish With Restricted Anterograde Transneuronal Viral Labeling and Quantitative Brain Mapping (PMID: 32038180)
phenotypes: Differences in topographical distribution of retinofugal connectivity patterns in dscaml1 mutants compared with wild type

biological.citation: Zebrafish dscaml1 Deficiency Impairs Retinal Patterning and Oculomotor Function (PMID: 31685652)
biological.summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 mutants showed deficits in retinal patterning and light adaptation. They also had oculomotor deficits (fatigue during gaze stabilization, reduced saccade amplitude and velocity, impaired fixation). Calcium imaging of abducens neurons showed impaired saccade-command signals, which suggests a defect in the saccadic premotor pathway. The phenotype resembles human ocular motor apraxia.

biological.citation: Tyrosine phosphorylation is essential for DSCAML1 to promote dendrite arborization of mouse cortical neurons (PMID: 24084194)
biological.summary: Knockdown of DSCAML1 in newborn mouse cortical neurons caused dendritic fasciculation and increased self-crossing, which impairs self-avoidance. The phosphorylation-deficient DSCAML1 Y1808F mutant failed to rescue the defect, so Y1808 phosphorylation is required for DSCAML1 function.

biological.citation: DSCAM and DSCAML1 regulate the radial migration and callosal projection in developing cerebral cortex (PMID: 25451118)
biological.summary: RNAi knockdown of DSCAML1 in mouse cortical neurons in vitro increased proximal dendritic branching complexity and impeded axon growth. In vivo knockdown impaired radial migration and callosal projection.

biological.citation: DSCAM and DSCAML1 function in self-avoidance in multiple cell types in the developing mouse retina (PMID: 19945391)
biological.summary: Dscaml1 is expressed in the rod circuit. Dscaml1-null mice had fasciculated rod bipolar cell dendrites and clumped AII amacrine cell bodies, which indicates a role in self-avoidance. Laminar stratification and rod-circuit synapse formation were intact, so Dscaml1 is not essential for synaptic specificity.

biological.citation: Nuclear import of the DSCAM-cytoplasmic domain drives signaling capable of inhibiting synapse formation (PMID: 30745319)
biological.summary: The DSCAML1 intracellular domain binds the importin IPO5 directly through a conserved nuclear localization signal and translocates to the nucleus. Expressing the DSCAML1 ICD altered expression of genes for neuronal differentiation, apoptosis and synapse function, and impaired neurite growth in primary cortical neurons. Unlike the DSCAM ICD, it did not reduce synapse numbers.

biological.citation: Cloning and functional characterization of DSCAML1, a novel DSCAM-like cell adhesion molecule that mediates homophilic intercellular adhesion (PMID: 11453658)
biological.summary: DSCAML1 (chr 11q23) encodes 10 Ig and 6 FNIII domains. It is a cell-surface molecule with homophilic binding activity that does not require divalent cations. In mouse brain it is expressed predominantly in cerebellar Purkinje cells, dentate gyrus granule cells, cortical neurons and olfactory bulb. In PC12 cells it targets axonal features.

biological.citation: Human down syndrome cell adhesion molecules (DSCAMs) are functionally conserved with Drosophila Dscam[TM1] isoforms in controlling neurodevelopment (PMID: 21645617)
biological.summary: Human DSCAML1 partially rescued the larval lethality of Drosophila Dscam mutants. It was targeted to dendrites and preferentially rescued dendrite defects, which shows functional conservation with the Dscam[TM1] isoforms.

biological.citation: Deficiency in the cell-adhesion molecule dscaml1 impairs hypothalamic CRH neuron development and perturbs normal neuroendocrine stress axis function (PMID: 36875755)
biological.summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 mutants had hypothalamic CRH neurons with higher crhb expression, increased cell number and reduced cell death. They also had higher baseline cortisol and attenuated responses to acute stressors, which implicates dscaml1 in HPA stress axis development.

biological.citation: Genetic effects of DSCAML1 identified in genome-wide association study revealing strong associations with litter size and semen quality in goat (PMID: 32036056)
biological.summary: Goat DSCAML1 expression in testis differed between the mitotic and meiotic stages. Three indels were genotyped in 2162 Shaanbei White Cashmere goats. Two indels (P2-16bp, P14-15bp) were associated with sperm motility and density, and three loci were associated with first-birth litter size. Genotype also affected DSCAML1 expression.

biological.citation: Expression patterns of dscam and sdk gene paralogs in developing zebrafish retina (PMID: 30078982)
biological.summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 was expressed in the inner nuclear layer and ganglion cell layer of the developing retina. Some cells in the basal INL co-expressed dscaml1 and dscama.
